title: Strings: immutability, characters, and frequency
summary: Treat strings as sequences with real costs, then use frequency maps and two pointers safely.

workedExample.title: Check a palindrome with two pointers
steps: Two indices begin at the ends. Each loop skips characters that are not letters or digits, because the problem says to ignore them.
After skipping, the characters at `left` and `right` are the next meaningful pair. Compare them case-insensitively.
A mismatch proves the string is not a palindrome, so return `false` immediately.
If they match, move both pointers inward. The process continues until the pointers meet or cross.
Each character is visited at most once, so the time is O(n). Only two integer indices are used, so extra space is O(1).

checkQuestions.prompt: What is the time complexity of building a string with `+=` in a loop for n total characters?
checkQuestions.explanation: Each concatenation copies the current accumulated string, so the total copied characters form 1 + 2 + ... + n.
optionExplanations: Only the final length is n; the copying is cumulative.
The work grows quadratically, not logarithmically.

checkQuestions.prompt: Why is a frequency array of size 26 useful for lowercase English letters?
options: It gives O(1) count updates and cache-friendly memory
checkQuestions.explanation: A fixed-size array maps each letter to a slot, making counts O(1) with no hashing overhead.
optionExplanations: A 26-slot array does not cover arbitrary Unicode.

options: The number of Unicode grapheme clusters
The number of UTF-16 code units
The number of bytes in memory
checkQuestions.explanation: `string.Length` counts UTF-16 `char` values, which may differ from user-perceived characters.
optionExplanations: Grapheme clusters can span multiple chars.
UTF-16 uses two bytes per code unit, so bytes are not the same as Length.
Words are not counted by Length.

complexityQuestions.prompt: State the time and space complexity of this method for a string of length n.
complexityQuestions.explanation: Each `+=` creates a new string and copies the previous characters, giving 1 + 2 + ... + n copies. The final string uses O(n) space, and old intermediate strings are garbage.

complexityQuestions.prompt: State the time complexity of this anagram check for strings of length n over a fixed lowercase alphabet.
complexityQuestions.explanation: Each string is scanned once. The count array has a fixed 26 slots, so extra space is constant with respect to n.

practice.title: Valid anagram
practice.prompt:
Given two strings `a` and `b`, return `true` if one is an anagram of the other. An anagram uses every character exactly the same number of times.

```csharp
bool IsAnagram(string a, string b)
```

Assume lowercase English letters for this exercise. State the complexity of your solution.
hints: If the lengths differ, what can you conclude immediately?
Use a count array indexed by `c - 'a'`. Increment for the first string, decrement for the second, and fail if any count goes negative.

practice.title: Longest common prefix
practice.prompt:
Given an array of strings, return the longest common prefix shared by all of them. Return an empty string if there is none.

```csharp
string LongestCommonPrefix(string[] words)
```
hints: Start with the first word as the candidate prefix. Compare it with each subsequent word and shorten it until it matches.
A simple approach compares character by character at each position across all words. Stop at the first mismatch or when a word ends. What is the worst-case complexity?
